Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic forecast errors and derive correction rules.

## Example 1 (2025-07-18)
History: Price has been range-bound around 70-73 since mid-June. Recent days show some volatility but no clear trend.
Sentiment: Mixed, with a few positive days (1.00, 0.67) on 71.93, 72.06, 71.51 etc.

Model forecast: Around 70.5-73.3 range
True outcome: Around 69.9-73.6 range

Looking at the differences:
- Model seems to be slightly too low on average in this example
- But let me look more carefully...

Actually, let me re-examine. The model forecasts in Example 1 are:
[69.96, 70.05, 69.47, 69.64, 71.10, 71.48, 70.79, 73.26, 73.14, 72.94, 71.46, 71.35, 71.91, 71.19, 71.78, 72.87, 71.88, 71.02, 71.20, 70.44, 70.36, 71.63, 71.22, 71.44, 72.85, 72.95, 72.83, 73.64, 73.57, 73.45]

True outcomes:
[69.89, 69.83, 69.11, 69.36, 70.88, 71.34, 70.65, 73.08, 72.86, 72.66, 71.04, 70.85, 71.59, 70.99, 71.77, 73.21, 72.37, 71.50, 71.74, 70.96, 70.68, 71.82, 71.16, 71.29, 72.62, 72.53, 72.19, 72.75, 72.24, 71.72]


I notice the model is underpredicting prices, particularly at the higher end of the range. When prices peak around 73.26-73.64, the model falls slightly behind reality. The divergence seems most pronounced
